title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
abstract: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $\pi$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.

title: Non-integer high harmonic generation from many-body nonadiabatic gating
abstract: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.

title: Origin of quadrupolar order in the 5d$^1$ double perovskite Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
abstract: Despite extensive experimental and theoretical studies of quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$, the microscopic origin and relative energy scales of the interactions driving it remain unresolved. In particular, the observed ferroic ordering of the $z^2$ quadrupole has remained difficult to explain, as the relative contributions of superexchange, classical quadrupole-quadrupole interactions, vibronic couplings, and virtual excitations to higher-energy levels have not been established quantitatively. Here, we determine all these interactions from first principles and solve the resulting microscopic Hamiltonian. The calculated ground state reproduces the experimentally observed quadrupolar order parameters and the associated structural distortions with quantitative accuracy. Disentangling the individual contributions, we find that ferroic $z^2$ order originates from a linear-quartic coupling, generated by virtual excitations to the $J_{\mathrm{eff}}$= 1/2 doublet and driven by vibronic interactions. Our results establish the hierarchy of microscopic interactions underlying quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and provide a unified $ab \ initio$ description of its coupled electronic and lattice degrees of freedom.

title: Ground state and thermal phase diagrams of the magnetized spin-$1/2$ XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice
abstract: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $\Psi$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$\Psi$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.

title: High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
abstract: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, $\epsilon_c = A\ln r_s + B + C r_s\ln r_s + D r_s + \dots$, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$ are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate $D$, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is $-0.0077880(9)$ Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of $-0.010$ Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order $r_s^2$, seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient $E_1$ sum to $(3.653 \pm 0.010)\times 10^{-3}$ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient $E_2$ sum to $\alpha^2(36\pi^2 - 208\ln 2 - 221)/(192\pi^4) \approx -1.433\times 10^{-4}$ Ha per electron, where $\alpha = (4/9\pi)^{1/3}$. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at $r_s = 0.5$ cannot distinguish between the two estimates of $D$.

title: A fermionic framework for quantum machine learning benchmarks
abstract: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.

title: Strong Co-O exchange interaction in $P4/nmm$ KCoO$_2$ and its effect on spin wave and N\'eel temperature
abstract: The exchange interactions of a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian in KCoO$_2$ in the $P4/nnm$ structure are calculated using a linear response approach, derived from the transverse spin susceptibility, integrated over atomic spheres using a projector proportional the local magnetization and including all atoms as magnetic atoms. The exchange interaction between Co and its apical O is found to be by far the largest interaction and ferromagnetic. Its effect on the N\'eel temperature and the spin wave spectrum are evaluated. The Co-O exchange is found to strongly enhance the critical temperature in the mean field approximation but not in the random phase approximation.

title: Spin Hamiltonian, magnetic anisotropy and excitation spectrum in altermagnetic $\alpha$-MnTe from first principles
abstract: The hexagonal altermagnet $\alpha$-MnTe combines a near-room-temperature collinear order with a strongly spin-split electronic structure, yet the microscopic origin of its easy-plane anisotropy, its zone-center magnon gap and its anomalously large magnetostriction have remained unexplained. We derive the complete low-energy magnetic Hamiltonian of $\alpha$-MnTe from first principles, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory with a force-theorem evaluation of the full anisotropic intersite exchange, single-ion terms and classical dipolar couplings. The isotropic exchange, including the altermagnetic splitting of the tenth-neighbor coupling, agrees with inelastic neutron scattering data. Contrary to the common single-ion picture, we find that the easy-plane anisotropy and the magnon gap at $\Gamma$ are governed by classical dipole-dipole interactions, which enhance the zone-center magnon splitting threefold leading to quantitative agreement with experiment, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term is irrelevant despite its size. The same Hamiltonian reproduces the chiral magnon splitting along antinodal directions, mirroring the electronic spin splitting, and quantitatively accounts for the giant magnetovolume coupling of $\alpha$-MnTe through the volume dependence of superexchange.

title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
abstract: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA). The method extends the Gutzwiller approximation by auxiliary ghost orbitals. It adds more of them whenever the correlations that build up during the dynamics exceed a threshold. This is computationally far more efficient than keeping their number fixed. As a demonstration we take the interaction quench of the half-filled Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. For this paradigmatic problem, numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) serves as the reference. A previous td-gGA study with a fixed set of 6 ghost orbitals per spin largely reproduced the available DMFT data. It lacked, however, an error estimate that would support predictions beyond them. With up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, adaptive td-gGA agrees with DMFT wherever DMFT data are available, from the weak-coupling prethermal regime to the strong-coupling collapse-and-revival regime. At strong coupling it remains converged up to three and a half times as long as the DMFT data. Near the crossover between the two regimes, the system relaxes to thermal values that agree with DMFT. Resolving the dynamics in the number of ghost orbitals shows how the sharp dynamical transition of the Gutzwiller approximation turns into this smooth crossover. In the extended time window at strong coupling, we observe that the oscillation frequency is renormalized as predicted by our second-order strong-coupling expansion. With its built-in error estimate, adaptive td-gGA offers a systematically improvable route to the extended-time dynamics of driven and multi-orbital correlated systems, especially when combined with tensor-network or quantum solvers for the embedding problem.

title: Universal spectrum of weakly coupled quantum critical Ising chains
abstract: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $\psi$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrm{\psi}$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrm{\psi}/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrm{\psi}$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.

title: Symmetry-dependent field-induced elastic renormalization in the quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy NiCoCr$_{0.8}$
abstract: We investigate the elastic response of cubic NiCoCr$_{0.8}$, a quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy, by high-precision ultrasound velocity measurements. At zero magnetic field, the three symmetrically independent elastic moduli $C_{11}$, $(C_{11}-C_{12})/2=C_t$, and $C_{44}$ monotonically harden upon cooling without pronounced elastic softening or anomalies. In magnetic fields applied along [110], however, a minute but systematic elastic renormalization of the order of $10^{-5}$ is resolved at low temperatures. The tetragonal $E_g$ mode $C_t$ softens with increasing field, whereas the derived bulk $A_{1g}$ mode $C_B$ hardens, revealing an opposite field response between the two strain-symmetry channels. Comparison with the previously reported quantum-critical-Fermi-liquid crossover scale shows that the field-induced elastic renormalization develops already in the quantum-critical regime and evolves continuously across the crossover region, without a sharp elastic anomaly or threshold behavior. These results demonstrate that symmetry-resolved ultrasound provides a sensitive probe of subtle strain-dependent changes in the electronic and magnetic free energy of a chemically disordered itinerant quantum-critical metal.

title: Curvilinear nanomagnets of non-trivial geometric topology
abstract: In this Chapter, we focus on the question of how the global geometric characteristics given by the topology of the sample's shape are reflected in the properties of the magnetization field of the given curvilinear nanoarchitecture. We start with a brief introduction to differential geometry and topology, giving their connection to the specific properties of the vector field represented by the magnetization field defined at the specific manifold. Then we discuss modern fabrication and characterization techniques that make analysis of a sample's topology not only an interesting theoretical concept but also a directly accessible and practically relevant topic. The main attention of the Chapter is dedicated to the theoretical and experimental analysis of nanostructrures with the topology different from the extended films beyond the in-depth studied topic of tubes of the constant radius. In particular, toroidal, spherical, and non-orientable manifolds are considered.

title: Contribution to the GdTe$_3$ magnetic phase diagram from electronic transport measurements
abstract: Magnetic phase diagrams of the three antiferromagnetic (AFM) transitions of GdTe$_3$ that occur at zero magnetic field at $T_{N1}=12$ K, $T_{N2}=10.5$ K and $T_1=7$ K are investigated by means of resistance measurements in a magnetic field oriented along the three crystallographic directions. With the magnetic field applied in the basal plane we found re-entrance of an intermediate phase which may be a result of the coupling between the $T_{N2}$ AFM and the charge density wave with possibly a ferroaxial order. A spin flop transition is also observed at a temperature that presumably converges towards a triple point in vicinity of 2.5-3.0 T and $T$ between $T_1$ and $T_{N2}$. Our results help complete a complex phase diagram of GdTe$_3$ and advance a method for investigating magnetic ordering via transport measurements -- a technique applicable to many other compounds.

title: Space-Time Point Defects as Probes of Criticality: Application to the Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg Transition
abstract: At criticality, a local field acting at a single point in Euclidean space-time is irrelevant and induces a modulation in space and time that decays with twice its scaling dimension. This turns two-point correlation functions into one-point measurements: one operator insertion enters the Boltzmann weight, the other is measured. For the local magnetization the relation is exact at any source strength. Implemented in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo, the approach yields the static spin susceptibility and imaginary-time-displaced correlations with unprecedented precision. We apply it to the Dirac-semimetal to antiferromagnetic-Mott-insulator transition of the half-filled $\pi$-flux Hubbard model. This lattice model provides a regularization of the $N_f=2$ Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg universality class. A finite-size scaling analysis estimates the critical exponents as $ \nu=1.10(3)$ and $\eta_\phi=1.09(4)$, close to field-theory predictions of $\eta_\phi\simeq1$. Since $\eta_\phi>1$, the equal-time structure factor at criticality does not diverge with the system size. Hence, the equal-time structure factor at the ordering wave vector is dominated by background contributions and cannot be used for extracting critical exponents. Consistently, the spin dynamics at the transition is strongly incoherent and the quantum Fisher information remains bounded.

title: Zone-folded Goldstone mode of the field-induced spin supersolid in the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet
abstract: The field-induced spin supersolid of the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet with single-ion and exchange anisotropy has so far been characterized only by static observables, among them a two-peak transverse structure factor. We compute its dynamic spin structure factors, and those of the neighboring phases, by stochastic analytic continuation of stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo data on a $16\times16$ lattice at inverse temperature $\beta=32$, at one field in each of the supersolid, the $m_z=1/2$ Ising plateau and the canted $XY$ phase. The supersolid has a single Goldstone mode, which the checkerboard folds onto both the ordering wave vector $\mathbf{Q}=(\pi,\pi)$ and $\mathbf{q}=(0,0)$, so that it appears in both spin channels at both points with one velocity $v=1.36\pm0.01$. The canted phase shows half of this pattern and the plateau none, the latter carrying instead a gapped magnon band and a two-magnon longitudinal continuum. Exactly at $\mathbf{Q}$ and $(0,0)$ the finite-lattice spectra are governed by a rotor tower of the condensate in the transverse channel and an Ising doublet of the checkerboard in the longitudinal one, both present at $\mathbf{Q}$ in the supersolid. Three parameter-free comparisons with the stiffness and the uniform susceptibility of the same runs, for the velocity, the sound-mode weight and the thermal decay of the rotor tower, tie the continued spectra to raw Monte Carlo observables. The folded Goldstone mode is the dynamical fingerprint of the supersolid.

title: Local Thermodynamic Reconstruction of Impurity Entropy
abstract: Resolving the thermodynamic entropy associated with a local impurity in a spatially extended interacting quantum bath remains a numerical challenge. We develop a Local-Maxwell approach that reconstructs the impurity entropy from local observables in worldline quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. By integrating their temperature responses along the impurity coupling, the method avoids separate estimates of extensive entropies. For nonnegative worldline expansions with bounded local couplings, we establish bath-size independent bounds on all factorial moments of the impurity vertex count. For even vertex counts, the Maxwell estimator variance remains bounded as the coupling approaches zero. The transverse-field Ising benchmark reproduces exact free fermion results, while an interacting XXZ chain demonstrates up to several hundredfold improvement in statistical efficiency over conventional extensive thermodynamic integration. In a three-channel XXZ impurity junction, we reveal entropy recovery upon cooling and a nonmonotonic coupling dependence of the finite-temperature entropy contrast. These results establish local thermodynamic reconstruction as an efficient approach to impurity entropy in interacting quantum baths.

title: Investigating competing order in the Kanamori-Hubbard model with the multiorbital multichannel fluctuating field theory
abstract: The multichannel fluctuating field (MCFF) approach treats selected collective fluctuations in interacting quantum lattice models nonperturbatively, but has so far been applied only to single-band systems. Here, we extend MCFF theory to multiorbital systems, accounting for the orbital structure of charge and spin instabilities. We apply it to the half-filled two-orbital Kanamori-Hubbard model with repulsive intra-orbital interaction $U$, and both positive and negative Hund's coupling $J$, addressing the competing orders and their interplay. The ability to selectively retain individual fluctuation channels and control their interplay allows us to disentangle their respective contributions and identify the mechanisms underlying competing instabilities. The model features a simple competition between charge density wave and antiferromagnetic fluctuations in the vicinity of $J=U$, and a more intricate competition between antiferromagnetic, orbital, and spin-orbital fluctuations near $J=0$, where the model acquires a higher SU(4) symmetry. The proposed multiorbital extension thus provides a computationally inexpensive and efficient framework for exploring how orbital and spin character shape competing collective fluctuations.

title: Signatures of Kitaev quantum spin liquid states in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ revealed by nitrogen-vacancy spin-noise spectroscopy
abstract: Bond-dependent magnetic interactions, strong spin-orbit coupling, and quantum fluctuations in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ make it an archetypical candidate for exotic Kitaev quantum spin liquid (QSL) states. While electronic transport, neutron scattering, optical and tunneling spectroscopies were used to probe global QSL signatures in large scale $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ samples, nanoscale evidence of local QSL behavior via a non-invasive experimental probe is still missing. Here, we use diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spin-noise spectroscopy to probe QSL states in {\alpha}-RuCl3 nanoflakes with thicknesses ranging from 8 to 150 nm over a temperature range of 4.3-250 K. Our measurements reveal a pronounced decrease in the NV spin-lattice relaxation time ($T_{1}$) below ~100 K in proximity to the $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ flakes, indicating enhanced GHz-frequency magnetic fluctuations. This temperature scale is consistent with the energy scale associated with Kitaev interactions (~8 meV) and the emergence of low-energy fractionalized excitations. Below 50 K, thicker (> 90 nm) flakes exhibit a distinct bi-exponential $T_{1}$ decay, unlike the single-exponential behavior observed for off-flake and thinner (8 nm) flake measurements, suggesting an increasingly heterogeneous magnetic noise environment. These results establish NV spin-noise spectroscopy as a local, non-invasive probe of low-energy spin dynamics in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ nanoflakes and open a route to testing predicted noise signatures of fractionalized excitations in atomically thin QSL candidates.

title: Absence of $\sigma$-criticality in Short-Range Spin Glasses
abstract: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of $\sigma$-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that $\sigma$-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called $\sigma$-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of $\sigma$-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of $\sigma$-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.

title: Conformality lost in Anderson localization in infinite dimensions, and regained in finite dimensions: a phenomenological theory of the Anderson transition in high dimensions
abstract: We show that the recent works on Anderson localization when the number of spatial dimensions $d\to\infty$ can be framed into the scenario dubbed it conformality lost [Kaplan et al., Phys. Rev. D 80, 125005 (2009)], which occurs when two fixed points of the RG collide and become complex. This framing makes it natural for a two-parameter scaling flow \`a la Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) to control all the observables of the theory as conjectured in [Vanoni et al., PNAS 121, e2401955121 (2024)]. We also use this as a starting point for an $\epsilon$ expansion of the RG equations in $\epsilon=1/d\ll 1$, and find phenomenological RG equations which fit the numerical results in dimensions $d\gtrsim 4$.

title: Moir\'e-enabled polariton control in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moir\'e bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moir\'e bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.

title: Moir\'e-Induced Interlayer Electron-Phonon Coupling in Graphene/hBN Superlattices
abstract: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moir\'e superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moir\'e potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moir\'e electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moir\'e superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moir\'e flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moir\'e electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.

title: Environmentally assisted transport in a diamond chain
abstract: We study quantum transport in a diamond chain coupled to Markovian reservoirs at its boundaries. The system is subject to uniform dephasing and an external magnetic field threading a flux $\Phi$ per plaquette. We derive exact analytical solutions for $\Phi=0$ and $\Phi=\pi$. We show that in the all-bands-flat regime at $\Phi=\pi$, dephasing destroys Aharonov-Bohm caging, leading to environment-assisted quantum transport. Our results demonstrate that coupling a flat-band system to a dissipative environment provides a viable route for controlling transport in regimes where coherent dynamics alone would result in complete localization.

title: Topological Narrow Bands in Twisted Rhombohedral Multilayer Graphene
abstract: Moir\'e graphene multilayers provide an atomically thin platform for engineering narrow topological bands through stacking, twist, and electrostatic control. Recent experiments on twisted rhombohedral graphene have revealed a high-Chern-number hierarchy determined by the number of rhombohedral layers. A microscopic description of this hierarchy requires connecting the ideal chiral picture to the realistic electronic structure. Here, we show that the two central moir\'e bands of twisted monolayer-$N$-layer rhombohedral graphene originate from hybridization between a monolayer Dirac cone and a rhombohedral surface state located at opposite corners of the moir\'e Brillouin zone. Increasing $N$ progressively narrows these bands, whereas reversing the displacement field transfers their wave-function weight between the twisted interface and the remote surface. In spectrally isolated regimes, this redistribution switches the lower band between Chern numbers $\mathcal{C}=N$ and $\mathcal{C}=-1$. A projected surface theory shows how interfacial tunneling is dressed by virtual propagation through the rhombohedral stack, explaining the field-selected Chern hierarchy and the recurring threefold structure of the real-space charge textures. These results establish layer number and displacement field as complementary nanoscale controls of band flatness, spatial polarization, and topology in graphene moir\'e heterostructures.

title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the {\pi}-conjugated spacers
abstract: The nature of the {\pi}-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca. 1,000), while those with a bithiophene spacer have a lower conductance switching ratio (ca. 500) at the stated conditions (light wavelength and intensity) and for one batch of samples (out of two). Similarly, the two former molecular junctions have quite similar trans-to-cis isomerization kinetics, while the latter has a lower switching rate. The energy level of the highest occupied molecular orbital, which controls the electron transfer in the molecular junction, is weakly influenced by the nature of the spacer, nor by the conformation of the azobenzene moieties. The large increase in the conductance of the molecular junction with azobenzene in the cis-state is explained by an increase in the electronic coupling energy between the molecule and the top electrode. Theoretical studies by Density Functional Theory and Non Equilibrium Green's Functions are qualitatively consistent with the experiments. We find a consistent structure-property trend, showing that the higher molecule/electrode coupling energy for the cis-state is explained by the top benzene ring of the azobenzene lying flat with respect to the top electrode for the thiophene, phenylthiophene and bithiophene spacers. On the contrary, we observe that a spacer with a carbon-carbon triple bond (acetylene thiophene) induces a large irreproducibility and unpredictability of the results.

title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
abstract: We study the scalar Schr\"odinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|\Omega_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|\Omega_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.

title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting is considered as one of the most promising approaches for the green hydrogen production. But the rapid recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs severely inhibits its photocatalytic efficiency. Construction of van der Waals heterostructures is a good way to suppress this recombination. However, in staggered band heterostructures, the charge transfer could occur either through the type-II or the direct Z-scheme mechanism. Therefore it is very important to identify which mechanism is dominant. In the present work, we systematically study the GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure using first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The system exhibits good thermodynamic, dynamic and thermal stability and an indirect band gap of 1.38 eV which greatly enhances the visible-light absorption. We find that the direct Z-scheme mechanism is the dominant interfacial charge transfer by analysing band alignment and Gibbs free energy pathways. The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) can be driven spontaneously in the pH range $4 \le \text{pH} \le 14$ under light irradiation for both type-II and Z-scheme pathways but the energy barrier is much lower for the Z-scheme mechanism. Moreover, the type-II mechanism is not suitable for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but the Z-scheme mechanism can promote HER well in the entire pH range ($0 \le \text{pH} \le 14$). Remarkably, the strain-free (pristine) condition exhibits a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 41.40\%, well above the 10\% threshold for commercial viability. The STH efficiency is further enhanced to 60.68\% under a tensile strain of +6\%. To summarise, the Z-scheme strain-tunable GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure is a promising and efficient photocatalyst for overall water splitting.

title: Emergent Electric-Field-Tunable $p$-Wave Magnetism in Twisted Bilayer NiPS$_3$
abstract: A perpendicular electric field can reorient a momentum-space spin texture without changing the local magnetic configuration. In this Letter, we investigate this mechanism in a $21^\circ$-twisted $\mathrm{NiPS}_3$ bilayer with zigzag order and coplanar, nonparallel layer N\'eel vectors. In the ideal nonrelativistic limit, an antiunitary in-plane half-translation enforces opposite-spin pairing at opposite momenta, while a layer-exchanging twofold operation pins the leading $p$-wave spin splitting to a crystallographic direction. A perpendicular layer bias lifts this orientational constraint while preserving the antiunitary symmetry, allowing a transverse component of the splitting vector. First-principles calculations show gate-dependent reorientation and deformation of spin-resolved isoenergy contours. Wannier-based linear-response calculations further reveal field-activated diagonal spin conductivities and a polarity-dependent tilt in the angular profile of the transverse spin-current response. The spin-texture axis, dispersion axes, and transport-response axis are distinct quantities governed by the same symmetry reduction. These results identify layer bias as a route to controlling odd-parity spin textures and spin-current anisotropy, provided that the coplanar magnetic state remains stable.

title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.

title: Comparative Molecular Dynamics Study of Initial Oxide Film Growth on Al, Mg, and Ti Using a Universal Neural Network Potential
abstract: Spontaneous formation of an oxide film, which may be passive, is found in many metals such as Al and Ti. We report direct computational observation of oxide film formation on the three major light structural metals, Al, Mg, and Ti, with molecular dynamics (MD) using a universal neural network potential (NNP). O2 molecules were supplied during MD simulations to replenish O consumed by the metal. Al and Ti formed a 1-2 nm thick film within a few ps of the simulation with O2 gas pressure of 102-103 atm. The film thicknesses of all metal oxides continued to increase proportionally to the logarithm of simulation time, consistent with Cabrera-Mott theory. Al and Ti oxides grow at the surface, while Mg oxide grows into the Mg metal. Al, Mg, and Ti are approximately 4.4, 4.3, and 5.2-fold coordinated, respectively, in the oxide.

title: A macroscopic-atom spectral theory of grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys
abstract: Predicting grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys remains challenging because existing spectral approaches require alloy-specific atomistic calculations to resolve segregation-energy distributions and correlations across non-equivalent boundary sites. Here, we develop a transferable macroscopic-atom spectral theory that predicts the joint segregation behavior of multiple species from physically interpretable elemental descriptors. The theory is founded on the finding that local strain and bond deficit account for 91\% of the site-to-site co-variation of 40 solutes in a density-functional-theory (DFT) Al polycrystal. Linked to atomic size and surface enthalpy, these coordinates allow prediction of individual segregation spectra and their cross-species correlations, which determine whether species compete for or share grain-boundary sites. A closed-system formulation unifies host-element redistribution and dilute-solute segregation, couples metallic and light-element sublattices, and accounts for bulk compound formation and solute pairing. Calibrated using binary spectra only, the theory predicts unseen-host spectral means with a correlation coefficient of 0.81, outperforms embedded-atom spectra against DFT benchmarks, and ranks site competition across 870 solute pairs with a Spearman coefficient of 0.90. Without fitting to multicomponent observations, it reproduces 11 of 12 equilibrium Fe ternaries and 49 of 55 Mg ternaries. Predictions recorded before simulations of an 82,699-atom polycrystal identify site competition as the baseline behavior and metal-metalloid pair chemistry as a source of deviations requiring atomistic resolution. These results establish a physically grounded route to screening grain-boundary chemistry in multicomponent alloys, including steels and high-entropy alloys.

title: Mixing and Preserving Properties of Non-van der Waals 2D Materials in Sandwich-like Heterostructures
abstract: Heterostructure interfaces created by stacking two-dimensional (2D) materials outline an appealing route towards achieving advanced electronic and magnetic functionalities at the nanoscale. Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) sandwich-like heterostructures (HSs) are build out of non-vdW 2D materials derived from non-layered crystals and establish a new frontier enabling strong interfacial coupling. Employing ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we investigate two classes of such trilayer HSs: purely non-vdW assemblies and hybrid vdW/non-vdW/vdW stacks. We show that non-vdW sandwiches undergo pronounced geometric reconstruction forming chemically bonded interfaces with large absolute binding energies up to an order of magnitude larger than those of conventional vdW HSs. These strong interactions drive extensive electronic hybridization, band gap renormalization, and tunable interlayer magnetic coupling. In contrast, vdW encapsulation largely protects the intrinsic atomic and electronic structure of the non-vdW sheet from the environment , while enabling charge transfer doping of the vdW layers. Our results thus establish sandwich HSs a versatile interface design platform, spanning interaction regimes from weakly perturbed encapsulation to strongly interacting chemically bonded systems with emergent electronic and magnetic behavior.

title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
abstract: Heat flow across the core-mantle boundary (CMB) depends on the lattice thermal conductivity ($\kappa_{\mathrm{latt}}$) of lowermost-mantle minerals, yet calculated CMB values for MgO differ severalfold, and high-temperature estimates of the conductivity increase across the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition range from about 20 to 50%. Direct solutions of the linearized phonon Boltzmann transport equation (LBTE) require thousands of density functional theory (DFT) force evaluations per thermodynamic state. Here we replace these evaluations with phase-specific, fine-tuned MACE potentials for MgO, MgSiO3 bridgmanite (Pv), and MgSiO3 post-perovskite (PPv). The potentials reproduce DFT energies, forces, stresses, pressure-volume relations, and compressed-state phonons for all three phases. For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes $\kappa_{\mathrm{latt}}$ by 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K. PPv is 44-55% more conductive than Pv at the same pressure and temperature and strongly anisotropic, with $\kappa_{[100]}/\kappa_{[010]}$ ranging from 1.7 to 2.1. The quasi-harmonic phase boundary has a Clapeyron slope of $(7.4 \pm 0.1)$ MPa/K and intersects a model geotherm at 116.2 GPa and 2660 K, where the transition raises the silicate conductivity by 47%, to 8.6 W/(m K). Heating in the basal thermal boundary layer lowers the MgO and PPv conductivities to 37.3 and 6.7 W/(m K) at the CMB, where Hashin-Shtrikman bounds of 9.5-11.4 W/(m K) for an Fe-free aggregate of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO encompass the 10 W/(m K) used in earlier heat-flow estimates. The density-temperature parameterizations provide an intrinsic end-member reference for lower-mantle thermal models.

title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
abstract: Native vacancy populations in transition-metal nitride coatings reflect vacancy formation, association, and depth-dependent stability. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compare these effects in rocksalt TiN and CrN in bulk and at (001) surfaces, within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges. In TiN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ is favoured under N-poor and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ under N-rich conditions; in CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ remains preferred throughout its stability range. Association energies are referenced to corresponding isolated vacancies where positive values mean association lowers the energy and negative values favour separation. Mean bulk association energies for mixed metal-nitrogen pairs are $+0.132$ eV in TiN and $+1.053$ eV in CrN. At (001) surfaces, $V_\mathrm{N}$ in TiN prefers the surface and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ the first subsurface layer. In CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ has similar formation energies at the surface and first subsurface layer, with a slight preference for the latter; $V_\mathrm{Cr}$ slightly prefers the second subsurface layer. Surface cluster energies are referenced to separated vacancies at their preferred depths. The compact $2V_\mathrm{Ti}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ cluster in TiN has favourable association in bulk ($+0.217$ eV per vacancy) but unfavourable association at the surface ($-0.346$ eV per vacancy). By contrast, $2V_\mathrm{Cr}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ in CrN remains stabilised, with its association energy decreasing from $+1.188$ to $+0.431$ eV per vacancy. CrN's stronger association occurs without larger structural distortions and is accompanied by distinct Cr-centred magnetic responses.

title: Band-Selective Coupling to Charge Density Wave Fluctuations in Kagome Superconductors AV3Sb5
abstract: The kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A=K, Rb, Cs) host multiband superconductivity (SC) within an unconventional charge density wave (CDW) parent phase, yet the relationship between the two remains unresolved. Through time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) experiments on CsV3Sb5 and KV3Sb5, we observe coherent band oscillations driven by coupling to a low-energy CDW amplitude mode at 3.1 THz. We find this coupling to be highly band-selective, differing by a factor of over 2 even between bands with dominant V-3d character. We reproduce these results with frozen-phonon density functional theory calculations, offering insight towards the relation between differing Fermi surface characters and our observed band selectivity. Furthermore, we observe differences in coupling channels between KV3Sb5 and CsV3Sb5. These results establish CDW amplitude mode fluctuations as a band-selective low-energy coupling channel that intimately contributes to the interplay between CDW and SC in the AV3Sb5 compounds.

title: Tunneling signatures of the Lifshitz transition in a superconducting vortex
abstract: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\sim\Delta^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.

title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
abstract: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

title: Majorana flat bands from mirror-particle-hole antisymmetry
abstract: Majorana flat bands, zero modes across the whole edge Brillouin zone, usually rest on chiral symmetry. We show that a fully gapped class-D superconductor can host such a flat band without chiral symmetry or time reversal, provided its superconducting gap is odd under a mirror and translation along the edge is preserved. Combined with particle--hole conjugation, the mirror forms an antiunitary antisymmetry that squares to $+1$ and preserves the momentum along the edge, so it fixes the Kitaev index of every slice of fixed edge momentum. In a gapped bulk, this slice index cannot change with the edge momentum, and the edge zero modes form a band across the whole edge Brillouin zone. We construct a four-band model with exactly these symmetries, a helical $p$-wave superconductor with Rashba coupling in an in-plane exchange field, from which no term can be removed without restoring an additional symmetry. On the mirror lines, its two mirror sectors are exact Kitaev chains. This yields a closed-form phase diagram. Besides the flat band, the model hosts a phase with two Majoranas at each end of a wire, although its class-D index is trivial, and a second-order phase with Majorana corner modes. The spectral localizer detects all these indices in real space, directly on finite-size samples as relevant for experiments. On open rectangular flakes of two widths, it reproduces the phase diagram even though translational symmetry is broken. In the nodal regions, its reading depends on the flake size, so they are left unread. The readings persist under disorder several times the bulk gap. Without translation along the edge, the symmetries protect no more than Majorana parities, and we quantify the signatures that remain specific to the antisymmetry. A minimal model of magnetic adatoms on a triplet superconductor realizes the flat-band and second-order phases.

title: Superconductivity with valley-imbalanced Fermi surfaces in thick rhombohedral graphene
abstract: Superconductivity in spin-polarized metals challenges conventional opposite-spin pairing, particularly when a magnetic field strengthens rather than suppresses it. In graphene, the additional valley degree of freedom broadens the possible pairing channels, making the valley occupation of the parent metal central to understanding such superconductivity. Here we report in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity in hBN-aligned 17-layer rhombohedral graphene. Normal-state quantum oscillations reveal unequal Fermi pockets consistent with a valley-imbalanced, spin-polarized parent metal. Calculations show that the parent electron pocket is predominantly localized on the bottom surface and largely preserved by electrostatic screening as additional Fermi pockets emerge. Superconductivity persists in this regime but is suppressed when carriers are polarized toward the hBN-aligned surface, where the parent bands undergo strong moire reconstruction. An adjacent nonlinear metallic response evolves continuously into superconducting critical-current features and persists above the superconducting transition temperature. The combination of valley imbalance and in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity motivates a phenomenological magnon-assisted equal-spin intervalley pairing scenario. These findings provide experimental constraints on pairing in valley-imbalanced metals and open a route to testing magnetic pairing mechanisms through layer-selective control of the parent electronic states.

title: Magnetoelectric response to a N\'eel domain wall in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films: Spontaneous currents, vortex pinning, and vortex-antivortex nucleation
abstract: We study the superconducting response induced by a N\'eel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectric coupling that induces spontaneous equilibrium currents. To establish the basic response to a continuously rotating magnetic texture, we first consider a periodic harmonic cycloid as an analytically tractable reference problem. Near Tc, this reference problem illustrates how the magnetoelectric coupling modifies the superconducting order parameter, while below Tc it provides a simple setting for describing the phase response, Pearl screening, and the interaction with a vortex. We then turn to the main problem of this work, a single N\'eel domain wall, and derive analytical expressions for its equilibrium phase profile, spontaneous current, magnetic field, and vortex-wall interaction energy.We show that the N\'eel wall acts as an extended magnetoelectric source and produces a vorticity-selective pinning landscape controlled by the competition between the wall width and the effective screening length. We further demonstrate that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can render a bound vortex-antivortex pair energetically favorable relative to the vortex-free state, even in the absence of an applied magnetic field. Our results provide an analytical framework for understanding magnetoelectric vortex pinning and vortex-antivortex nucleation by N\'eel domain walls in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films.

title: From Fermions to Vortices: Microscopic Simulations of Phase Ordering in a d-Wave Superconductor
abstract: Describing bath-induced superconducting phase ordering directly from a microscopic fermionic Hamiltonian remains a formidable challenge. Here we develop a microscopic framework for this problem using the recently introduced adiabatic variational principle (AVP) and demonstrate its application to a two-dimensional $d$-wave superconductor. The central construction maps evolving, spatially inhomogeneous bond-pairing fields onto constrained Bogoliubov-de Gennes states, with the associated Lagrange multipliers determining the thermodynamic driving forces. This enables dissipative evolution of the superconducting order while retaining its microscopic electronic structure, without assuming a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functional. Starting from disordered pairing configurations, we resolve the emergence of phase coherence through vortex-antivortex annihilation and the accompanying evolution of local electronic spectra. Vortex decay and dynamical scaling recover the characteristic kinetics of two-dimensional phase ordering, providing a nontrivial benchmark of the framework. The solver-independent AVP formulation opens a route to microscopic studies of dissipative ordering and metastability in superconductors with intertwined stripe and pair-density-wave orders.

title: Topological Anderson Superconductor in Landau Levels
abstract: There is much interest in two-dimensional superconductors with odd integer values of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Chern number $C_{\rm BdG}$, often termed topological superconductors, as these are predicted to harbor Majorana zero modes. Because a magnetic field produces Landau levels (LL) with nonzero Chern numbers, it is natural to ask if a conventional two-dimensional superconductor of spinful fermions with Rashba spin-orbit coupling can be driven topological by application of a magnetic field. Self-consistent solutions of the BdG equations for an on-site attractive interaction produce a phase diagram consisting almost everywhere of superconducting states with even integer values of $C_{\rm BdG}$, transitioning from one value to another as parameters such as the chemical potential are varied. We predict that introducing Anderson-type on-site disorder, which broadens as well as mixes LLs, produces, in the transition region, states wherein topological superconductivity percolates. This topological Anderson superconducting state provides another example where disorder can produce topologically nontrivial states.

title: Multistable Thermoelectric Josephson Automata
abstract: Multistable systems can store and process information, yet their elements usually only burn the drive energy. Here, we build an automaton whose elements actively convert heat into electrical power. Heat alone stabilizes the states at zero bias, and each state routes generation and dissipation to different junctions. The elements, gap-asymmetric superconducting tunnel junctions, deliver up to 2.6 pW at either polarity under fixed heating and support a magnetic-field-tunable Josephson current. Two junctions sharing a heated island split the bias hysteretically and, even at zero bias, lock into opposite voltages encoding the sweep direction. With a load and current bias, the automaton accesses states spanning junction polarity combinations, including zero voltage; the magnetic field sets which are available and the bias history selects the occupied one.

title: Imaging Compressible and Incompressible Kinetic Energy of a 2d Bose-Einstein Condensate
abstract: We introduce a method based on velocity-sensitive two-photon transitions to reconstruct the two-dimensional velocity field as well as the local atomic density of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a single realization. We quantitatively benchmark the method on a quantized vortex. Applied to a condensate far from equilibrium, the method reveals the contrasting behaviors of the system's flow kinetic energy components, where the compressible component quickly decays while the incompressible one remains, dominating the long-time dynamics.

title: Detecting Topological Phases Through Dynamics of Chiral Density in Momentum-space Lattices
abstract: Momentum-space lattices offer a versatile platform for quantum simulation in particular emulating topological states of matter.In this work, we propose a spectroscopic protocol via utilizing the dynamics of the chiral operator to detect the topological properties of a momentum-space Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain. We show that the time evolution of the chiral density is directly linked to the local density of state (LDOS). By performing a Fourier transformation of that, we reconstruct both the LDOS and density of states of the system, enabling the unambiguous signature of zero-energy edge modes and the bulk-boundary correspondence. This dynamical approach provides a diagnostic tool for exploring topological phases in synthetic quantum matter.

title: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
abstract: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons, provides a microscopic description of strongly interacting matter, including hadron structure and dynamics. Real-time dynamics and finite-density properties of these systems remain challenging for conventional Monte Carlo methods because of sign problems. Quantum simulation provides a complementary approach, although circuit depth and noise limit digital implementations and non-Abelian gauge-matter interactions remain difficult to engineer in analog systems. Here we realize a non-Abelian lattice gauge model with dynamical matter in an analog cold-atom simulator and directly observe its hadronic dynamics using site- and spin-resolved quantum gas microscopy. This realization is enabled by harnessing two hyperfine states and site-occupation configurations of 87Rb atoms to jointly encode both matter and gauge fields. We tailor resonant tunneling in a spin-dependent optical superlattice to implement a gauge sector of a truncated one-dimensional SU(2) quantum link model with independently tunable mass and gauge coupling. Leveraging this control, we track the conversion of an initially mesonic state into baryonic or vacuum-like configurations through slow mass ramps. Near resonance, we observe coherent oscillations between mesons and baryon-antibaryon pairs and characterize the conversion efficiency as a function of mass, gauge coupling and net baryon density. Our realization establishes an atomic platform for non-Abelian gauge dynamics, opening a route to microscopic studies of nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly interacting matter.

title: Relaxation dynamics of the impurity momentum in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
abstract: We consider a single mobile impurity coupled by a repulsive contact interaction to a gas of free spinless fermions of equal mass in one dimension. Using the determinant overlaps between the interacting eigenstates and free-fermion states, we derive closed determinant formulas for the matrix elements of the impurity momentum operator and of its square between arbitrary Bethe-ansatz eigenstates of a finite system. At infinite coupling we prove a selection rule: both operators have vanishing matrix elements between distinct eigenstates that share the same rapidity, and every eigenstate carries the per-particle share of the total momentum. For an impurity injected into the Fermi sea we have the following: at infinite coupling the average impurity momentum relaxes completely in the thermodynamic limit, while at finite coupling relaxation remains incomplete. The closed-form matrix elements turn the spectral representation of the average impurity momentum into explicit finite sums over eigenstates. We evaluate the post-injection dynamics, resolve the quantum-flutter oscillations and the approach towards the diagonal-ensemble value, and map the stationary momentum as a function of the injection momentum and the coupling. Finally, we analyse the thermodynamic limit and its asymptotics as an integral over Fredholm determinants.

title: Probing the Rung-Mott Insulator in Bosonic Two-Leg Ladders
abstract: Mott insulators typically appear at integer densities, but certain lattice geometries or non-local interactions can stabilise Mott insulators at fractional densities. In this work, we study strongly interacting two-leg ladders using ultracold bosonic atoms around half-filling, and identify the rung-Mott insulating (RMI) phase through its characteristic rung occupation in site-resolved measurements. We probe its excitation spectrum via lattice modulation spectroscopy, and interpret the observed spectra using numerical simulations that include the driven dynamics, coupling to multiple excited states, and energy offsets. As with other Mott insulators, the RMI phase is characterized through its incompressibility, which we probe via a site-resolved analysis of densities and chemical potentials. Our results provide direct insight into the excitation dynamics of a strongly correlated ladder system, and pave the way for studying transport and further dynamical properties in low-dimensional quantum systems with programmable lattice geometries.

title: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line
abstract: A one-dimensional model of a Bose-Fermi mixture with contact repulsions is exactly solvable via nested Bethe ansatz. That formal solution is here simplified along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested. The model solution is expressed in terms of the known solutions for the Lieb-Liniger model and the Yang-Gaudin model of attractive spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ fermions in the balanced case. We find explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, the velocities of excitations, and the Drude weights at weak and strong interactions. At weak interactions, the special line corresponds to the parameter values where the isolated systems of free fermions and weakly interacting bosons have equal velocities.

title: Parametric neural-network wavefunctions across a bosonic phase transition
abstract: We propose Boseformer, a universal attention-based neural-network architecture for representing the wavefunctions of particles with bosonic quantum statistics, including superfluid and crystal phases. The model is trained to generate the wavefunction as a function of a Hamiltonian parameter across the quantum phase transition between these phases. Once trained with variational Monte Carlo optimization, it can serve as a foundation model describing the phase transition without the need to retrain it for individual parameter values. We demonstrate our method on a system of two-dimensional bosons with $1/r^3$ repulsive interaction.

title: A machine learning architecture for scaling of holographic quantum circuits
abstract: We describe an architecture and workflow for learning and generalizing the syntax and parameters of holographic quantum circuits (HQCs), which are natural quantum circuit analogs of classical tensor networks. An HQC uses mid-circuit measurements and resets on a small subset of "physical" qubits whose measurement outcomes become correlated through coupling with a register of persistent "ancilla" qubits, analogous to the physical and bond indices of a tensor network. Hence, an HQC with fixed qubit resources can efficiently generate samples from a large quantum state, and adding qubits to the HQC ansatz has the effect of exponentially increasing the effective bond dimension. Our machine learning approach provides mechanisms for harnessing both features of HQCs by extrapolating the syntax (e.g., a sequence of gates, measurements, and resets) and parameters (e.g., the angles appearing in single-qubit rotations) from a dataset of HQCs to longer or more expressive HQCs. We demonstrate the methodology and its performance on an analytically solvable dataset formed by a vector-valued generalization of the W-state. Finally, we provide an outlook for usage of the methodology for scaling the effective bond dimensions of HQCs in quantum simulation.

title: Transfer tensor description of driven inhomogeneous quantum systems
abstract: The transfer tensor method (TTM) extrapolates open quantum system dynamics from short-time trajectories by encoding memory effects in a discrete hierarchy of transfer tensors. Standard TTM relies on time-translational invariance (TTI) of the dynamical maps, which is broken by time-dependent driving or coherent control. We generalize TTM to time-inhomogeneous and periodically driven systems with a two-time transfer tensor hierarchy $\mathcal{T}(n,k)$. For driving with period $t_0$, sub-stroboscopic sampling ($\Delta t = t_0/N_c$) restores a block TTI, $\mathcal{T}(n+mN_c, k+mN_c) = \mathcal{T}(n,k)$, so that only $N_c$ starting-time branches must be learned. Averaging over the driving phase (or start time), termed temporal homogenization, restores single-index TTI at the price of phase-induced memory that combines non-additively with that of static disorder. We study two systems. (i) In an inhomogeneously broadened two-level ensemble driven beyond the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), the phase-induced memory scales with the square of the Rabi coupling and the disorder-induced memory with the square of the inhomogeneous width. The phase-induced memory is frame dependent: in the drive's rotating frame it arises solely from counter-rotating terms and vanishes under the RWA, whereas in the lab frame it largely survives the RWA. (ii) In a driven tight-binding chain at the Dunlap--Kenkre condition, the clean chain is stroboscopically frozen, whereas sub-stroboscopic tensors show that dynamical localization is enforced by delayed, period-commensurate refocusing in the memory kernel, in contrast to the immediate backflow of Anderson localization. A generalized outgoing pseudoflux tracks the non-monotonic dependence of the spreading on disorder: moderate disorder breaks the refocusing and lets the particle spread over a larger but finite region, whereas strong disorder confines it.

title: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps
abstract: Finding the ground states of quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge in physics and quantum chemistry. Imaginary-time evolution (ITE) offers a natural, widely used route, but its convergence is typically asymptotic. Variational approaches restrict this evolution to parameterized manifolds, with neural quantum states (NQS) providing flexible representations commonly optimized via stochastic reconfiguration (SR). Their performance depends on the geometry of the variational manifold, the convergence properties of ITE, and the stability of finite-step explicit (forward) integrators. By exploiting local geometric information of the energy landscape, the recently introduced augmented imaginary-time evolution (AITE) can, in principle, reach the ground state in finite imaginary time. To exploit the accelerated convergence of AITE in NQS optimization, we first combine an implicit Euler step with Galerkin projection to derive an implicit SR scheme that permits large, stable steps and substantially outperforms conventional methods. We use it to formulate an implicit version of AITE and show that its acceleration persists under variational projection and finite-step integration with asymptotically quadratic convergence of the energy error. With finite sampling, implicit schemes yield consistent gains, and implicit AITE becomes increasingly advantageous.

title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
abstract: Noise in quantum devices remains a major challenge for reliable quantum simulations, making quantum error mitigation an important tool for improving their accuracy. Machine learning-based quantum error mitigation (ML-QEM) provides a useful approach, but its performance depends on the training datasets and may produce reconstructed quantum states that are not physically valid. In this work, we introduce an ML-QEM framework that uses residual learning with convex projection to ensure that reconstructed density matrices satisfy physically valid density matrices. We study the effect of different training datasets and regression models using Haar-random and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansatz states. We compare the proposed approach with conventional ML-QEM, readout error mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation. The method is tested on IBM quantum hardware for three- and four-qubit simulations of the bound $\Lambda$-deuteron and $\Lambda$-$\alpha$ hypernuclear systems, respectively. For the three-qubit system, ridge regression trained on VQE-ansatz states gives a ground-state energy of -0.134 MeV, close to the ideal value of -0.135 MeV, with a state fidelity of 0.999. For four-qubit system, kernel ridge regression gives ground-state energies of -3.014 and -3.045 MeV, with corresponding state fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998. These results show that physically constrained reconstruction, along with the choice of training datasets and regression models, can improve ML-QEM performance for the quantum simulations studied in this work.

title: Current-Dependent Meta-GGA and Local Hybrid Functionals for Relativistic NMR Shifts
abstract: NMR chemical shifts are key for the characterization of novel compounds. Especially for molecules with heavy elements, the experimental data is often corroborated with computational studies in density functional theory (DFT). However, modern meta-generalized gradient approximations (meta-GGAs) and local hybrid functionals are not widely supported in relativistic calculations with quantum chemistry program suites. So far, their current-dependent generalization in the spirit of Dobson, Becke, and Tao was not presented at all. This generalization ensures gauge invariance and does not introduce artifacts--unlike the more popular field-dependent generalization of the kinetic-energy density. In non-relativistic and scalar-relativistic calculations, the first was shown to be superior but the current density only arises due to the magnetic field perturbation. In contrast, spin--orbit coupling also induces current densities in the preceding ground-state calculation and the DFT framework needs to be generalized to a current density functional theory (CDFT) for consistency with the current-dependent response equations. Herein, we present the two-component relativistic generalization of the current-dependent kinetic-energy density of a Kramers-restricted Kohn--Sham reference for meta-GGAs and local hybrid functionals in NMR calculations. The extension is invariant under a position-dependent phase and a position-dependent spin rotation of the spinors, or a local U(1)$\times$SU(2) transformation. Relativistic effects are considered with exact two-component theory using a superposition of atomic potentials to include the two-electron picture-change correction (SAP-X2C).

title: OMNI-P3x universal neural network potential for large-scale computational photochemistry workflows
abstract: Computational photochemistry supports the design and understanding of new materials. However, the high cost of excited-state quantum-mechanical (QM) calculations makes screening large molecular libraries prohibitively expensive. To address this limitation, we introduce OMNI-P3x, a universal machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) for singlet ground- and excited-state simulations of neutral and charged organic molecules. Trained on both ground- and excited-state conformations, it performs complete computational photochemistry workflows with accuracy approaching TD-DFT. We demonstrate its practical applicability by screening a combinatorial library of 234,375 flavylium derivatives, where the pretrained model performs ground-state geometry optimization and predicts absorption properties without additional QM calculations. Following fine-tuning, we further screen 162,960 xanthene-based dyes, identifying new candidates for red, near-infrared and short-wavelength infrared emission. Furthermore, state-dependent neural charges, learned without reference atomic charges, provide an interpretable picture of intramolecular charge redistribution upon excitation.

title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
abstract: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine-tune molten-copper and water potentials against experimental diffusion coefficients together with structural constraints. For water, jointly optimizing diffusion and the oxygen-oxygen radial distribution function also improves the predictions of shear viscosity and rotational relaxation, neither of which is included in the optimization objective. Alignment at a single temperature also improves the apparent activation energies of multiple dynamical observables, bringing their temperature dependences closer to experiments. Moreover, the optimized potential exhibits smaller force errors relative to an independent, higher-level quantum-chemical reference, indicating that alignment with experiments improves the fidelity of the potential energy surface beyond the fitted targets. PathGrad thus establishes a general framework for incorporating experimental observables directly into force field optimizations.
